hypothesis: The shared video unit core reproduces the decoder and encoder bindings' behavior, and the native VE preparation matches the vendor VeReset instructions for all admitted identities.
conclusion: The composed software path matches the reference; hardware is not qualified.
narrative: checks/a733-video-unit.c (removed as a fixture whose runners were removed) drove the JPEG and H.264 decoder bindings and both encoder bindings through nominal, cold-start, identity, contention, uncertain-write, refused-mutex, parent-selection and job-mismatch cases, recording every callback, register access and clock observation. The recorded digests matched those of the separate decoder and encoder implementations that preceded the shared core, and the encoder native checks produced identical programmed writes and encoded pictures. checks/a733-video-platform-reference.py (removed: it needs the vendor libVE.so, libawh264.so and libawmjpeg.so, which are not in the source or input caches) executed the original libVE.so VeReset instructions with the matching policy-table index and recorded reference and native preparation traces. Kernel reset operations were explicitly modeled from cedar_ve.c and ccu_reset.c; hardware reset effects were not simulated. Complete final register images and ordered reset pulses matched for all three admitted identities. The gate-status correction preserved the previously compared preparation writes byte for byte, and AArch64 compilation passed with warnings as errors. The original reviewed source and evidence are frozen under review-20261016, and the effective-gate correction under review-gates-20261016; both preserve the exact external media-clock dependency used to compile and execute the checks. Source, fixtures, binaries, reference input hashes and results remain outside Git with SHA256 manifests. The component check used the preserved baseline fixture and current native parser source; it does not reconstruct the earlier JPEG malformed-input run (see video-codecs).
